## Final Accepted Amendments

### `fr-5-0fe11abb`

CleanFilter action (engine.rs:353-373) reduces microbe biomass by `intensity * 0.5` across all four guilds but does not route the removed biomass to dissolved organics or detritus. The element content (N and C) of the cleaned-off biomass silently vanishes. The budget guard masks this because `action:clean_filter` is listed as an open-system action in `tick_has_closed_system_nitrogen`. Fix: route the setback biomass to dissolved organic pools (same pattern as `route_live_biomass_to_dissolved_organics` in nitrogen_cycle.rs), and either remove `action:clean_filter` from the open-system exclusion list so the guard can verify conservation, or record an explicit export entry in the budget ledger.

### `fr-5-2e08bd46`

In `crates/tank_core/src/engine.rs`, make the closed-system budget guard depend on actual mass movement, not just the presence of an action label. Every queued action is recorded into the tick ledger (`step_one_hour`, lines 93-99), but several of the actions that are treated as open-system in `tick_has_closed_system_nitrogen`/`tick_has_closed_system_carbon` can be no-ops (`Feed { grams: 0.0 }`, `WaterChangePercent { percent: 0.0 }`, `SiphonDetritus { fraction: 0.0 }`, `CleanFilter { intensity: 0.0 }`, `AddShrimp { count: 0 }`, `RemoveShrimp { count: 0 }`; see `process_action`, lines 285-406). Because `tick_has_closed_system_nitrogen` only checks `entry.label` (`engine.rs`, lines 523-544), any such zero-effect action suppresses the conservation guard for that tick even though the tick is still closed. Use `BudgetEntry.delta` (or the original action parameters) so zero-delta/no-op actions do not disable the nitrogen/carbon balance check.
